items.title: fix(guards): the Bash doors read a multi-line command, a heredoc and an unbalanced quote
items.why: reproduced on main 7f8a0d7 in a scratch copy: segments('true\ngit push --force origin x') is one argv and the heredoc case returns []; six doors pass a second-line command; a security finding, fixed in public
items.promise: guards.segments() ends a command at a newline outside quotes, drops a heredoc body as data (reads it as commands when the heredoc feeds sh, bash, zsh or dash), joins a backslash-newline line continuation before splitting, and a command shlex cannot tokenize is refused when its raw text names a door program (git push, gh pr, gh api, gh repo, wuwei hook, the ledger path). Touches cli/wuwei/guards.py (segments, bash, the module docstring that says an unreadable command passes) and tests/test_guards.py. Outside: python -c and other interpreter bodies, here-strings, any new door. The runtime stays at most 3,000 lines: the added lines come out of guards.py itself (one _git helper for origin and current_branch, about -2; the two ledger refusals in bash() folded into one check, about -2; the rest from guards.py or hook.py, never from evidence.py, gh.py or setup.py, which 1067 and 1065 net against).
acceptance: given 'true\ngit push --force origin x', when the Bash door reads it, then the force-push door refuses

given "cat > b.md <<'EOF'
it's done
EOF
gh pr create -F b.md" and the gates missing at the branch head, when the Bash door reads it, then the create door reads the create and refuses
given an unclosed quote in a command that also runs 'gh pr merge 5', when the Bash door reads it, then it refuses and names the unreadable command as the reason

given 'git push \\\n  --force origin x' (a line continuation), when the Bash door reads it, then the force-push door refuses (the newline split must not cut a continued line: probed, a naive split loses --force)
given "bash <<'EOF'\ngit push --force origin x\nEOF", when the Bash door reads it, then the force-push door refuses
given 'git commit -m "a\nb" && git push origin feature', when the Bash door reads it, then the quoted newline stays in the message and nothing is refused
given an ordinary multi-line command with no door program, including one with an unbalanced apostrophe, when the Bash door reads it, then nothing is refused
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: fix(doctor): the hooks check counts any hook that fired on this machine since init
items.why: a false 'doors are off' while the create door refused a PR and a plan: answer was recorded (#1064 session); the check reads one file only SessionStart writes
items.promise: wuwei doctor reports ok hooks when .wuwei/executable exists or when this clone's own ledger file (.wuwei/ledger/<ws.clone(root)>.jsonl) holds a row only a hook writes (refused, asked, note, prompt, seat.started, seat.stopped, stop.reminded, hook.error) after its latest workspace.init. attest and sent do not count: the CLI writes them too. Rows synced from another clone do not count: the ledger travels on wuwei/state, so another machine's hook says nothing about this one. Touches cli/wuwei/setup.py (doctor) and tests/test_setup.py. Outside: the hook events, traces.jsonl (written only with telemetry on). Lines come out of setup.py: doctor reads ws.config(root) twice (lines 125 and 133, -1) and settings.json is parsed in three places (lines 36, 64, 150).
acceptance: given a workspace after init with a refused row in this clone's ledger file and no .wuwei/executable, when doctor runs, then it reports ok hooks
given a hook-only row only in another clone's ledger file, when doctor runs, then it reports warn hooks
given a hook-only row older than the latest workspace.init and no .wuwei/executable, when doctor runs, then it reports warn hooks
given .wuwei/executable written by SessionStart, when doctor runs, then it reports ok hooks as today
given the change, when the suite runs, then the runtime size test still passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: fix(evidence): a commit status posted by a review-triggered workflow reads as review, not CI
items.why: six ai-stacks PRs needing a reviewer show 'CI running [waiting]', and #3274 reads as a red build; build after 1067-probe, since the tie between status and workflow is unmeasured
items.promise: A commit status posted by a workflow the repository runs on pull_request_review is reported as 'waiting on review: <context>' (pending) or 'change request outstanding: <context>' (failure), both actionable safety gaps, instead of 'CI running' or 'CI failing'. The review-triggered workflows come from the host, not config: repos/<repo>/actions/runs?event=pull_request_review, cached for a day, read only when the head has a commit status; the tie from status to workflow is the one 1067-probe finds (target_url run id or the context equal to the workflow name). Touches cli/wuwei/gh.py (pr: status target_url, the review-workflow read), cli/wuwei/evidence.py (ci_gaps), tests/test_evidence.py, docs/design.md section 6 and docs/site/concepts/evidence.md. Outside: CODEOWNERS and required reviews (#917), a config key. Lines come out of evidence.py and gh.py (evidence.py line 214 re-imports datetime inside budget, -1), never from guards.py or setup.py.
acceptance: given completed check runs and a pending commit status from a workflow the repository runs on pull_request_review, when evidence reads the PR, then it reports 'waiting on review: <context>' as actionable and no 'CI running'
given that status failing while a change request stands, when evidence reads the PR, then it reports 'change request outstanding: <context>' and no 'CI failing'
given a failing status from an ordinary CI workflow, when evidence reads the PR, then it reports 'CI failing: <context>' as today
given a head with no commit statuses, when evidence reads the PR, then no workflow-runs call is made
given the workflow-runs read fails, when evidence reads the PR, then the status stays CI (never a pass)
given either review gap, when the merge door runs with or without --auto, then it refuses
given the change, when the suite runs, then config still has five keys and the runtime size test passes at 3,000 lines or fewer

items.title: probe: what ties ai-stacks' Review Gate status to its review-triggered workflow
items.why: 1067 is the riskiest item: its whole design rests on a host shape nobody here can read (ai-stacks returns 403 to this session); a pending state set before any review cannot come from a pull_request_review run, so the run event alone may not classify it
items.promise: A run, not a change: from a session with read access to A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks (this one has none: HTTP 403, add_repo needed), read three REST endpoints at the head of ai-stacks#3300 and #3274 and record the answer with wuwei plan run 1067-probe --reason. Endpoints: repos/A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks/commits/<head>/status (the Review Gate status: context, state, target_url, creator), repos/A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks/actions/runs?head_sha=<head> (event, path, name and id of each run), repos/A-Teams-Network/ai-stacks/actions/runs?event=pull_request_review&per_page=100 (the review-triggered workflow names and paths), and .github/workflows/review-gate.yml's on: block. Outside: any code change.
acceptance: given read access to ai-stacks, when the probe reads the Review Gate status at #3300's head, then it records whether its target_url names a workflow run and which run

given the runs at that head, when the probe reads them, then it records the event of the run that set the pending state (pull_request_review, pull_request or another) and whether the workflow name equals the status context

given neither the target_url nor the context ties the status to a review-triggered workflow, when the probe ends, then 1067 is reshaped before any build (a scope: question to the owner, since a sixth config key is out)
items.reason: probe answered: target_url run id -> workflow path -> on: names pull_request_review; run event alone does not classify
